0.headline: Five drafts, zero points, 114 on every single table
0.overview: Thirty-nine days, twenty-one picks, and right now — dead even. Every one of these five drafts sits at 0 pts with 114 on the table, so the only thing to judge is the shape. Tami drafted from the front of the snake and walked away with Jelly at #1, then bagged a fifth body at #21 where only her best four count. Taylor and Kylie went early-round star power. Tim built a theme and stuck to it. Austin, picking last in the snake, got squeezed at the top and hunted value in the middle rounds. Nobody's been voted out. Everybody's still dreaming.

lines.text: Picking dead last in the snake order, Austin never touched the top four, so he built "Livestock and Lenses" out of Linnea and Jenna at #5 and #6 and then doubled down in the middle with Carter and Eric — a roster with no headliner and no obvious hole.

Kylie grabbed Aaliyah at #3 and then quietly assembled the most varied résumé board in the draft — a chef, a Head of HR, a criminal defense attorney, and a game designer — four people who all talk for a living, and Kilby at #18 is the pick everybody else scrolled past.

Tami had the #1 pick, took Jelly, and then worked both ends of the snake all the way down to Rob at #20 — and because she holds five with only her best four counting, Sharonda at #21 is a free insurance policy nobody else in this family gets.

Taylor opened with 49-year-old Kristin at #2 — the oldest name off the board early — then went pure engine room with Ori, Ana, and pro wrestler Brady at #19, and "Crisis, Cardio and Chaos" is exactly what that roster looks like.
Tim took Lewis at #4 and Maggie at #7, two farmers back to back, then added an actor and a medical student — "The Charm Farm" is the most committed bit in the draft and Tim did not blink once.

awards.label: Boldest draft
awards.text: Spending picks #4 and #7 on two farmers is a swing nobody else in this family had the nerve to take.

awards.label: Safest draft
awards.text: Four picks spread from #5 to #16 with no reaches and no gimmick — Austin drafted the board exactly as it fell to him.
